title.zh: 卷四十四 志第十四: 曆象志下
title.raw: 卷四十四 志第十四: 曆象志下 Volume 44 Treatises 14: Celestial Phenomena 3

sentences.zh: 曆象誌下 ○朔考

translations.literal: Treatise on Calendars and Celestial Signs, Part Three ○ Study of New Moons
translations.idiomatic: Celestial Phenomena, Part Three — New Moons

sentences.zh: 古者太史掌正歲年以敘事，國史以事系日，以日、月、時系年。

translations.literal: In antiquity the Grand Clerk controlled setting the year aright to narrate affairs; the state chronicle tied affairs to days, and tied days, months, and seasons to the year.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times the Grand Astrologer set the civil year so the court could record events in order; the national chronicle linked each affair to its day, and days, months, and seasons to the year.

sentences.zh: 時月不正，則敘事不一。

translations.literal: When seasons and months are not correct, narration is not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: If the seasons and months are wrong, the historical record falls out of step.

sentences.zh: 故二史合為一官，頒歷授時，必大一統。

translations.literal: Therefore the two clerks were combined into one office; issuing calendars and bestowing the seasons must achieve great unity.
translations.idiomatic: For that reason the two chronicle offices were merged into one, charged with issuing calendars and marking the seasons under a single standard.

sentences.zh: 遼、漢、周、宋，俱行夏時，各自為歷。

translations.literal: Liao, Han, Zhou, and Song all observed Xia calendar times yet each made its own calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Liao, Later Han, Zhou, and Song all followed the Xia seasonal scheme, but each maintained its own calendar.

sentences.zh: 國史閏朔，頗有異同。

translations.literal: Intercalation and new moons in the national chronicles differed considerably.
translations.idiomatic: Their intercalary months and new-moon dates often disagreed.

sentences.zh: 遼初用《乙未元曆》，本何承天《元嘉曆》法，後用《大明曆》，本祖沖之《甲子元曆》法。

translations.literal: At first Liao used the 《Yiwei Origin Calendar》, based on He Chengtian's 《Yuanjia Calendar》 method; later it used the 《Daming Calendar》, based on Zu Chongzhi's 《Jiazi Origin Calendar》 method.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao first adopted the 《Yiwei Origin Calendar》, derived from He Chengtian's 《Yuanjia Calendar》, and later the 《Daming Calendar》, derived from Zu Chongzhi's 《Jiazi Origin Calendar》.

sentences.zh: 承天日食晦朏，一章必七閏；

translations.literal: He Chengtian: solar eclipses on the last or first of the month, one era always seven intercalations;
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian placed eclipses on month-end or month-begin and required seven intercalary months in every era;

sentences.zh: 沖之日食必朔，或四年一閏。

translations.literal: Zu Chongzhi: solar eclipses necessarily on the new moon, sometimes one intercalation in four years.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi insisted eclipses fall on the new moon and allowed an intercalary month as seldom as once in four years.

sentences.zh: 用《乙未曆》，漢、周多同；

translations.literal: Using the 《Yiwei Calendar》, Han and Zhou mostly agreed;
translations.idiomatic: On the 《Yiwei Calendar》, the Later Han and Zhou usually matched;

sentences.zh: 用《大明曆》，則間與宋異。

translations.literal: using the 《Daming Calendar》, then occasionally differed from Song.
translations.idiomatic: on the 《Daming Calendar》, they sometimes diverged from the Song.

sentences.zh: 國史敘事，甲子不殊，閏朔多異，以此故也。

translations.literal: In state chronicle narration, sexagenary days did not differ, but intercalation and new moons often differed—for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: In the annals the sexagenary day-counts agree, but intercalary months and new moons often do not—and that is why.

sentences.zh: 耶律儼《紀》以《大明》法追正《乙未》月朔，又與陳大任《紀》時或抵牾。

translations.literal: Yelü Yan's 《Annals》 used the 《Daming》 method to correct the 《Yiwei》 months and new moons, and sometimes clashed with Chen Daren's 《Annals》.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Yan's 《Annals》 retrofitted 《Yiwei》 new-moon dates with the 《Daming》 system, which sometimes conflicts with Chen Daren's 《Annals》.

sentences.zh: 稽古君子，往往惑之。

translations.literal: Scholars examining antiquity are often perplexed by this.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars who weigh the past are often left puzzled.

sentences.zh: 用《五代職方考》誌契丹州軍例，作《朔考》。

translations.literal: Following the method of the 《Five Dynasties Administrative Geography Study》 to record Khitan prefecture and army examples, the 《Study of New Moons》 was composed.
translations.idiomatic: Following the model of the 《Five Dynasties Administrative Geography Study》, this 《Study of New Moons》 records Khitan prefectures and garrisons.

sentences.zh: 法殊曰「異」，傳訛曰「誤」；

translations.literal: When methods differ it is marked 「variant」; when transmission is corrupt it is marked 「error」;
translations.idiomatic: A difference in calendrical method is marked 「variant」; a corrupt transmission is marked 「error」;

sentences.zh: 遼史不書國，儼、大任偏見並見各名；

translations.literal: The Liao History does not write state names; Yan's and Daren's biased views both appear under each name;
translations.idiomatic: The Liao History omits state labels; Yan's and Daren's partisan readings both appear under each entry;

sentences.zh: 他史以國冠朔。

translations.literal: other histories prefix new moons with the state name.
translations.idiomatic: other histories prefix each new moon with the reigning state.

sentences.zh: 並見註於後。

translations.literal: Both appear in the notes below.
translations.idiomatic: Both conventions are explained in the notes that follow.

translations.literal: (See the book, pages 568–677, which contain tables.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Tables appear on pages 568–677 of the printed edition.)〉

sentences.zh: 高麗所進《大遼事跡》載諸王冊文，頗見月朔，因附入。

translations.literal: The 《Great Liao Affairs》 presented by Goryeo records the investiture documents of the princes and often shows month and new moon; therefore it is appended.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo's tribute text, the 《Great Liao Affairs》, preserves princely investiture edicts with many month-and-new-moon dates, and so it is included here.

sentences.zh: ○象

translations.literal: ○ Phenomena
translations.idiomatic: ○ Instruments and Omens

sentences.zh: 孟子有言：「天之高也，星辰之遠也，茍求其故，千歲之日至可坐而致。

translations.literal: Mencius said: 「Heaven is so high, the stars so far—if one earnestly seeks their causes, the solstice of a thousand years hence can be seated and reached.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius said: 「Heaven is so high and the stars so distant that, if you truly seek their principles, you can sit where you are and calculate the solstice a thousand years from now.

sentences.zh: 」甚哉，聖人之用心，可謂廣大精微，至矣盡矣！

translations.literal: 」How vast! The sage's intent may be called broad and subtle—utterly complete!
translations.idiomatic: 」What breadth and fineness of mind the sages showed—nothing left beyond their grasp!

sentences.zh: 日有晷景，月有明魄，鬥有建除，星有昏旦。

translations.literal: The sun has gnomon shadows, the moon bright and dark phases, the Dipper has Establishment and Removal, stars have dusk and dawn.
translations.idiomatic: The sun casts measurable shadows, the moon waxes and wanes, the Dipper marks the seasonal nodes, and the stars have their risings and settings.

sentences.zh: 觀天之變而制器以候之，八尺之表，六尺之筒，百刻之漏，日月星辰示諸掌上。

translations.literal: Observing heaven's changes, they made instruments to await them—an eight-foot gnomon, a six-foot tube, a hundred-mark clepsydra—so sun, moon, stars, and constellations were shown on the palm.
translations.idiomatic: They watched the sky's motions and built instruments to track them—eight-foot gnomons, six-foot sighting tubes, hundred-division water clocks—until sun, moon, and stars could be read as if on the palm of the hand.

sentences.zh: 運行既察，度分即審，於是像天圜以顯運行，置地櫃以驗出入，渾象是作。

translations.literal: Once motion was investigated and degrees and minutes verified, heaven was imaged in a sphere to display motion and an earth cabinet was set to test ingress and egress—the armillary sphere was made.
translations.idiomatic: When their measurements of motion were secure, they cast a celestial globe to show the heavens turning and fitted an earth cabinet to test risings and settings—the armillary sphere was born.

sentences.zh: 天道之常，尋尺之中可以俯窺，陶唐之象是矣。

translations.literal: The constant of heaven's Way can be peered into within a foot's measure—such was the image of Yao's Tao Tang.
translations.idiomatic: The regularities of heaven could be inspected within a few feet—such was the celestial model of the age of Yao.

sentences.zh: 設三儀以明度分，管一衡以正辰極，渾儀是作。

translations.literal: They set up the three armillaries to clarify degrees and minutes and piped one balance to correct the celestial pole—the equatorial armillary was made.
translations.idiomatic: They mounted the three rings to fix degrees and minutes and aligned a sighting tube to the pole—the observational armillary was made.

sentences.zh: 天文之變，六合之表可以仰觀，有虞之璣是矣。

translations.literal: Astronomical changes across the six directions' surface could be looked up at—such was the jade sight-rule of Yu's era.
translations.idiomatic: The shifting heavens across the four quarters could be viewed directly—such was the sighting instrument of the age of Shun.

sentences.zh: 體莫固於金，用莫利於水。

translations.literal: No body is firmer than metal; no use is more apt than water.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing is sturdier than metal for structure, nothing more versatile than water for motion.

sentences.zh: 範金走水，不出戶而知天道，此聖人之所以為聖也。

translations.literal: Casting metal and running water, knowing heaven's Way without leaving the door—this is how the sage became sage.
translations.idiomatic: By casting bronze and channeling water they could know heaven's Way without leaving the hall—that is what made the sages sages.

sentences.zh: ○刻漏

translations.literal: ○ Clepsydra
translations.idiomatic: ○ Water Clocks

sentences.zh: 晉天福三年造。

translations.literal: Made in the third year of Tianfu of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: It was built in the third Tianfu year of the Later Jin.

sentences.zh: 《周官》契壺氏，懸壺必爨之以火。

translations.literal: In the 《Rites of Zhou》, the Pitcher-Kettle office—hanging pitchers must be heated with fire.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Rites of Zhou》 describe the Pitcher-Kettle officers, who always warmed the suspended vessels with fire.

sentences.zh: 地雖沍寒，蓋可施也。

translations.literal: Though the land is frozen cold, it can presumably be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Even in bitter frost the method can still be used.

sentences.zh: ○官星

translations.literal: ○ Official Stars
translations.idiomatic: ○ Star Officials

sentences.zh: 古者官星萬餘名。

translations.literal: In antiquity there were more than ten thousand star-official names.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity named more than ten thousand stellar offices.

sentences.zh: 遭秦焚滅圖籍，世秘不傳。

translations.literal: They were burned when Qin destroyed the records, and the age kept them secret without transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's burning of the archives destroyed them, and later ages kept what survived hidden.

sentences.zh: 漢收散亡，得甘德、石申、巫咸三家圖經。

translations.literal: Han gathered what had scattered and perished, obtaining the star charts of the three houses of Gan De, Shi Shen, and Wu Xian.
translations.idiomatic: The Han recovered what survived and obtained the celestial maps of Gan De, Shi Shen, and Wu Xian.

sentences.zh: 經緯合千餘官，僅存什一。

translations.literal: Longitude and latitude together yielded more than a thousand officials—only one tenth remained.
translations.idiomatic: Their combined catalogs listed more than a thousand stars—only a tenth of the ancient names survived.

sentences.zh: 分為三垣、四宮、二十八宿，樞以二極，建以北斗，緯以五星，日月代明，貴而太一，賤逮屎糠。

translations.literal: They were divided into the Three Enclosures, Four Palaces, and Twenty-eight Mansions; pivoted on the two poles, established on the Northern Dipper, woofed with the Five Stars; sun and moon alternate in brightness; the noble reaches Supreme One, the base down to chaff and dung.
translations.idiomatic: They were arranged into the Three Enclosures, Four Palaces, and Twenty-eight Mansions, anchored on the celestial poles and the Northern Dipper, woven through the five planets; sun and moon take turns in glory, from the exalted Supreme One down to the lowliest chaff.

sentences.zh: 占決之用，亦云備矣。

translations.literal: For purposes of divination and judgment, it may also be said to be complete.
translations.idiomatic: For divination the system was already more than adequate.

sentences.zh: 司馬遷《天官書》既以具錄，後世保章守候，無出三家官星之外者。

translations.literal: Sima Qian's 《Treatise on the Heavenly Offices》 already recorded them fully; later generations of observers never went beyond the star officials of the three houses.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian's 《Treatise on the Heavenly Offices》 preserved the full roster, and later court astronomers never looked beyond the three classical star catalogs.

sentences.zh: 天象昭垂，歷代不易，而漢、晉、隋、唐之書累誌天文，近於衍矣。

translations.literal: The heavenly signs shine down and hang forth, unchanged through the ages, yet the books of Han, Jin, Sui, and Tang repeatedly recorded astronomy—nearly redundant.
translations.idiomatic: The heavens themselves do not change, yet Han, Jin, Sui, and Tang histories piled up repeated treatises on astronomy until the subject grew redundant.

sentences.zh: 且天象機祥，律格有禁，書於勝國之史，詿誤學者，不宜書。

translations.literal: Moreover, heavenly signs and omens have regulations with prohibitions; writing them in the history of a conquered state misleads scholars and ought not to be written.
translations.idiomatic: Heavenly omens are governed by strict rules; to set them down in the annals of a fallen dynasty only misleads students, and so they should not be recorded here.

sentences.zh: 其日食、星變、風雲、震雪之祥，具載《帝紀》，不復書。

translations.literal: Solar eclipses, stellar anomalies, winds, clouds, thunder, and snow omens are fully recorded in the 《Imperial Annals》 and are not written again here.
translations.idiomatic: Eclipses, strange stars, winds, clouds, thunder, and snow are already given in full in the 《Imperial Annals》, and are not repeated in this treatise.
